items.title: Verifier, config builder, and UI units have no dependency edges
items.statement: LSPS-097 defines the registry implementation, LSPS-098 defines configuration and dispatch, and LSPS-099 defines the controls, but each unit has an empty dependency list. The core therefore does not require compile or rollout ordering, nor prove that every configured method has a registered verifier and every UI field reaches the dispatch consumer.
items.impact: A configuration can be persisted or criteria emitted without a usable registry entry, producing a dead control or an unhandled verification method.

items.statement: The nested config is named and fields are preserved, but the authoritative behavior does not define defaults, validation, precedence, enable/disable transitions, scope grammar, block_on combinations, tier-boundary normalization, timeout bounds, or what happens to stored values when the gate is disabled.
items.impact: Different consumers can accept contradictory configurations and produce inconsistent gate decisions.

items.title: Verifier failure taxonomy and recovery are unspecified
items.statement: The verifier calls the diagnostics API and returns only passed, message, and evidence. The core does not distinguish a clean diagnostic result from timeout, client absence, crash, cancellation, malformed response, partial path resolution, or stale diagnostics, and it does not define retry, fallback, or fail-open/fail-closed behavior.
items.impact: Infrastructure failure can be misreported as a successful or failed code-quality gate and can promote or block work incorrectly.

items.title: lsp and lsp_gate alias semantics are ambiguous
items.statement: Registration under lsp or lsp_gate does not state whether both aliases must always be registered, whether one is canonical, how collisions are handled, or whether stored configurations migrate between aliases.
items.impact: Existing settings or criteria can stop dispatching when implementations choose different aliases.

items.title: Verification controls have no effective-state or save-failure truth
items.statement: Binding and same-blob persistence are required, but the core does not define disabled or unavailable states, validation feedback, dirty state, save-in-progress, save failure, rollback, conflict resolution, or how the UI proves the value currently used by the gate.
items.impact: The tab can display a saved or enabled gate while runtime uses a rejected, stale, or unavailable configuration.

items.title: Opening full runtime artifacts has no authorization boundary
items.statement: The user may explicitly open the full runtime artifact, but no actor, project membership, workspace trust, policy, or confirmation requirement governs that escape from summarization-only mode.
items.impact: A user or injected interaction may expose raw diagnostic and trace material beyond the intended prompt cap.

items.title: Top-five selection is nondeterministic
items.statement: Current relevance or severity supplies neither a total ordering nor precedence, tie-breaking, stable recomputation, deduplication, or a definition of an evidence item. The same evidence set can therefore yield different prompt inputs.
items.impact: Gate explanations and model behavior become irreproducible, and important errors may be displaced by arbitrary ordering.

items.statement: A maximum of five items does not constrain bytes, tokens, message length, diagnostic cardinality inside an item, trace size, or the size of a full artifact. The snapshot object likewise admits an unbounded diagnostics array.
items.impact: A small item count can still exhaust context, memory, disk, serialization time, or UI rendering capacity.

items.title: Diagnostic and snapshot data have no privacy lifecycle
items.statement: Paths, project roots, diagnostic messages, sources, codes, and trace material can contain repository structure, source excerpts, usernames, or secrets, but the core defines no classification, redaction, encryption, file permissions, retention, deletion, export, or prompt-ingestion consent rules.
items.impact: Sensitive local data can persist indefinitely on disk or enter prompt context and full-artifact views without policy controls.

items.title: Untrusted diagnostic fields lack validation and rendering rules
items.statement: The schema lists path, message, source, and code but does not bound length, define code type, normalize paths, reject control characters, escape markup, distinguish absolute from project-relative paths, or prevent malicious diagnostic text from becoming prompt instructions or UI content.
items.impact: A language server or repository-controlled analyzer can cause path traversal, log or UI injection, prompt injection, denial of service, or misleading evidence.

items.title: Character-coordinate protocol semantics are missing
items.statement: The diagnostic schema stores character, but the conversion decision covers only line values. It does not define whether character is UTF-16 code units, UTF-8 bytes, Unicode scalar values, or grapheme clusters; whether it is 0- or 1-based in evidence; or where conversion occurs.
items.impact: Diagnostics after non-ASCII text can point to the wrong location, and different clients can serialize incompatible evidence.

items.title: Line conversion lacks invalid and overflow behavior
items.statement: The 1-based evidence rule does not specify rejection or normalization of zero, negative, missing, non-integer, or overflowing line values, nor how unknown positions are represented. A mechanical subtract-one conversion can underflow or turn invalid data into a valid-looking location.
items.impact: Malformed server data can crash conversion or create false navigation targets.

items.impact: Concurrent or interrupted gate runs can overwrite, truncate, or misattribute evidence while leaving a valid-looking path.

dimension_assessments.summary: Registry, criterion builder, persistence, and UI consumers are named but not dependency-bound or end-to-end required.
Configuration state, ranking transitions, and invalid coordinate handling are underspecified.
Snapshot writers have no collision, atomicity, or concurrent-cleanup contract.
LSP absence, timeout, malformed and partial responses, cancellation, and stale diagnostics are not distinguished.
Neither config persistence failures nor partial snapshot writes have rollback or recovery semantics.
The full-artifact escape hatch and snapshot deletion authority have no actor or policy guard.
Sensitive paths, roots, messages, traces, and snapshots lack redaction, consent, permission, retention, and deletion rules.
Language-server fields and filename identifiers lack validation, escaping, bounds, and containment.
The tab has no contract for unavailable, dirty, saving, failed, conflicted, or effective runtime states.
The LSP client unavailable and timeout behaviors are not mapped to gate or UI state despite a preserved when_unavailable token.
Five items is not a byte or token bound, and snapshot count, diagnostic count, artifact size, and retention are unbounded.
No semantic, keyboard, focus, announcement, or non-color contract accompanies the user-visible controls and evidence.
No localization boundary separates product copy, formatted coordinates and timestamps, and verbatim server messages.
Alias migration, config defaults, character encoding, unknown enums, and snapshot schema evolution are not defined.
Result and snapshot data lack correlation, producer, revision, configuration, completeness, and schema-version metadata.
Persistent evidence has no governed cleanup, confirmation, reference safety, or failed-deletion behavior.
Preserved ContractRefs are not connected to concrete PlanUnits, fields, versions, dependency edges, or bidirectional checks.
The listed acceptance and validation surfaces test governance lineage rather than the required runtime, UI, failure, security, and persistence behaviors.
Future server diagnostic variants and extension fields have no negotiation or preservation strategy, leaving behavior intentionally unresolvable from this core.
